name: Konni Elephant Training Centre
tagline: Kerala’s historic Aanakoodu — elephants, museum and forest ecotourism
summary: Historic forest-department elephant camp at Konni with the 1942 Aanakoodu, an elephant museum and ecotourism programmes; visitors can watch feeding, bathing and conservation briefings (confirm before…
description: Konni Elephant Training Centre (Anathavalam / Aanakoodu) is a long‑established Forest Department elephant camp near Konni town in Pathanamthitta district. The site centres on a large traditional wooden kraal (built 1942), a small museum and forest‑department visitor facilities.

The centre plays a conservation and rescue role: orphaned or injured calves are cared for, mahout training and kumki training happen under department supervision, and the campus demonstrates traditional elephant husbandry alongside modern veterinary care.

For visitors the centre offers close views of the elephants, feeding/bathing demonstrations, an interpretation/museum area (includes a tusker skeleton display) and eco‑shop products. Programmes, bookings and public access are run by the Kerala Forest Department ecotourism unit — always confirm availability before you plan a trip.
Konni pairs well with nearby Adavi ecotourism (Kallar river coracle rides) and local waterfalls, making it a useful base for a half‑day or full‑day nature visit in Pathanamthitta.
highlights: Historic Aanakoodu (wooden elephant kraal) built in 1942
Elephant museum with skeletons and interpretation panels
Forest Department‑run feeding (anayoottu), bathing and guided talks
Conservation and kumki training activity (department programmes)
Combine with Adavi coracle rides and nearby waterfalls

sections.heading: Background
body: Konni’s elephant tradition dates back centuries; the present Aanakoodu structure was built in 1942 and is part of the Kerala Forest Department’s elephant care and training programme. The camp historically sheltered rescued calves and trained kumki elephants used for managing conflict situations.

Today the site functions as a mix of rescue/rehabilitation, mahout training and an ecotourism visitor destination managed by the Forest Department; conservation, veterinary oversight and visitor education all form part of the programme.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Watch the elephants during supervised feeding and bathing demonstrations, visit the elephant museum (tusker skeleton and displays), and buy local forest products at the eco‑shop. Guided conservation talks explain the Forest Department’s work with rescued calves and kumki training.

Programmes vary by season and by the department’s operational decisions; some activities (close contact, rides) have been restricted in recent seasons for safety and welfare reasons, so check current offerings with the Konni Divisional Forest Office or the official ecotourism booking portal before visiting.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best months are in the cool, dry season (roughly October–March) when river and forest activities and most ecotourism programmes run. Confirm opening hours, ticketing and safety notices with the Konni forest office or the Kerala Forest Ecotourism booking site before you go.

Konni sits about 10–12 km from Pathanamthitta town; allow a half‑day if you combine the camp with Adavi coracle rides or nearby waterfalls. Follow Forest Department instructions on photography and distance from animals.

latest.text: Local reporting notes the Forest Department is planning additional kumki training centres in the state and lists Konni as a possible location; no final official announcement was published at the time of the report.

Kerala Forest Ecotourism listings and online booking pages for Konni (Anathavalam/Elephant Kraal) show elephant‑feeding and museum packages available in October 2026, indicating visitor programmes are being offered via the department portal (confirm date‑specific slots before travel).

Independent travel guide updated 25 Sep 2026 cautions that public entry to the Aanakoodu had been stopped after a fatal accident in April 2025 and advised travellers to confirm access with the Divisional Forest Office; this note remains relevant when checking current access.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Cool, dry season — roughly October to March (confirm specific programme dates before travel).
visitorInfo.howToReach: By road: Konni is about 10–12 km from Pathanamthitta town (local buses and taxis). Nearest major railhead: Chengannur (≈34 km). Nearest airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport (≈100–110 km).
etiquette: Always confirm programme availability and booking with the Konni Divisional Forest Office or the Kerala Forest Ecotourism portal before you travel.
Follow staff instructions at all times; do not approach elephants or cross safety barriers for photos or feeding.
Treat the visit as educational: ask about rescue, veterinary care and kumki training — welfare standards and permitted activities change, so confirm current rules.
Combine the camp with Adavi coracle rides or nearby waterfalls to make a full half‑ or full‑day trip.
